name: Gaimberg
kurzbeschreibung: Mountain village above Lienz with breathtaking views of the Dolomiten and the Iseltal.
beschreibung:
Overview

Gaimberg is situated in the sun-drenched Lienz Basin in East Tyrol, extending along the gently rising southern slopes of the Zettersfeld at the foot of the Schober Group. The charming municipality borders directly on the district capital of Lienz to the south and, with an area of just 7.28 square kilometres, is one of the smallest municipalities in the district. Approximately 850 residents live across the peaceful settlements of Grafendorf, Obergaimberg, Untergaimberg, Wartschensiedlung, and Postleite. Together with neighbouring Oberlienz and Thurn, Gaimberg forms the renowned holiday region of the Lienz Sun Villages, celebrated for its mild microclimate and extraordinary sunshine hours. From the hillside terraces, visitors enjoy sweeping views of the craggy limestone peaks of the Lienz Dolomites, including Große Sandspitze, Spitzkofel, and Laserzwand.

History

Human settlement on these sunny slopes dates back to antiquity: excavations in Grafendorf in 1935 unearthed the foundations of a Roman villa rustica along with bronze figurines, indicating close ties to the nearby Roman town of Aguntum. The name Gaimberg originally designated the entire sunny mountain face north of Lienz, with individual farmsteads documented from 1380 onward in registers of the Counts of Görz. The administrative heart was established by the noble knights of Grafendorf; the 1352 seal of knight Chunrat Swenter featuring a green dragon head on a gold field serves as the municipal coat of arms today. The spiritual core of the village is the parish church of St. Bartholomew in Grafendorf, first recorded in 1411. Its Late Gothic choir was completed in 1534, redesigned in the 19th century, and restored to Gothic style in 1934; notable highlights include historic frescoes, altarpieces by Karl Untergasser, and the historic walled cemetery.

Getting There

By car, travellers reach Gaimberg from the north via Kitzbühel and the Felbertauern Road B108 leading directly into Lienz. From the east via Carinthia, the route follows the Tauern Autobahn A10 to Spittal an der Drau and continues along the Drautalstraße B100 to the town, while guests from South Tyrol arrive via Innichen and Sillian. From downtown Lienz, the provincial road L321 reaches Gaimberg and the valley station of the Zettersfeldbahn in just a few minutes. Rail passengers arrive at Lienz in Osttirol station aboard ÖBB regional trains from Spittal an der Drau or San Candido. From the station forecourt, scheduled VVT buses and the Lienz city bus serve Gaimberg, complemented by free winter ski shuttles.

Tips

The premier highlight is the hiking and family ski area of Zettersfeld, whose gondola valley station lies within Gaimberg and whisks visitors up to over 1,800 metres above sea level. In winter, sun-drenched pistes, a fun park, and welcoming huts offer panoramic skiing against the backdrop of the Dolomites. In summer, the Zettersfeld Family Park features interactive discovery stations, while hikers tackle the scenic trail to the crystal-clear Neualpl Lakes at 2,436 metres or the summit of Schleinitz. Owing to its warm climate, Gaimberg maintains a proud fruit-growing and distilling heritage; a visit to the modern distillery at Obsthof Webhofer offers tastings of award-winning schnapps and organic juices. Culture lovers can take a relaxing stroll along the signposted village circular trail past traditional farmsteads and historic chapels.
